title: Where to store this data
question: Which Google Cloud service should hold this data?
quickRule: Start with how the data is read and written, then pick the service built for that access pattern.

options.name: BigQuery
options.chooseWhen: You need to analyze large amounts of data with SQL. It fits business intelligence, ad hoc analysis and machine learning.
options.beCarefulWhen: Your data already lives in Bigtable or Spanner. BigQuery can query it there, so you may not need to copy it.

options.name: Bigtable
options.chooseWhen: You need high read and write throughput at low latency on large amounts of single-keyed data. It fits time series, IoT and clickstream data.
options.beCarefulWhen: Your app is small. The docs say Firestore may suit small applications better, and the row key needs careful design.

options.name: Spanner
options.chooseWhen: You need a relational database with SQL, strong consistency and horizontal scale. It supports transactions at large scale.
options.beCarefulWhen: You create the database. You must choose the GoogleSQL or PostgreSQL dialect then.

options.name: Cloud SQL
options.chooseWhen: You want a managed MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server database. The docs call it the easiest lift and shift to the cloud.
options.beCarefulWhen: You need virtually unlimited scale. Each Cloud SQL instance is powered by a virtual machine, so compare Spanner.

options.name: Firestore
options.chooseWhen: You build mobile or web apps with flexible documents. It is serverless and can sync data, also offline.
options.beCarefulWhen: You need analytics over all your documents. Load the data into BigQuery for that.

title: Dataflow, the Spark service or Cloud Data Fusion
question: Which service should run this data processing job?
quickRule: Dataflow for new batch and streaming code, Spark for existing Spark jobs, Data Fusion for visual pipelines.

options.name: Dataflow
options.chooseWhen: You need batch and streaming pipelines at scale. It is fully managed and uses Apache Beam.
options.beCarefulWhen: You have Spark or Hadoop jobs today. Dataflow runs Apache Beam pipelines, but the Spark service moves Spark projects without redevelopment.

options.name: Managed Service for Apache Spark (formerly Dataproc)
options.chooseWhen: You have Spark or Hadoop jobs to move to Google Cloud. Use clusters for deep control or serverless for new pipelines.
options.beCarefulWhen: You choose clusters. They give more control but they are your infrastructure to manage, while serverless needs no cluster.

options.name: Cloud Data Fusion
options.chooseWhen: You want to build ETL or ELT pipelines with a visual, point-and-click tool. It needs little or no code.
options.beCarefulWhen: You run a pipeline. By default Data Fusion creates a Spark cluster for each run, so you also depend on the Spark service.

title: Pub/Sub or Managed Service for Apache Kafka
question: Which messaging service should carry these events?
quickRule: Pub/Sub is the simple default on Google Cloud. Choose Kafka when you need Kafka compatibility or portability.

options.name: Pub/Sub
options.chooseWhen: You want a serverless service with little to manage. It scales on its own, also when your workload size changes.
options.beCarefulWhen: You need Kafka compatibility. Pub/Sub is a distinct service with its own API.

options.name: Managed Service for Apache Kafka
options.chooseWhen: You have Kafka workloads to move with few code changes. It also fits when you need the same API across clouds or on-premises.
options.beCarefulWhen: You pick it. You must manage capacity, such as the cluster size and the number of partitions.

options.name: Both, joined with Kafka Connect
options.chooseWhen: Some of your systems use Kafka and others use Google Cloud services. Kafka Connect connectors can link a Kafka cluster to Pub/Sub and BigQuery.
options.beCarefulWhen: You mix the two. Kafka clients and Pub/Sub clients are not interchangeable, because Pub/Sub has its own API.

title: Managed Airflow, Workflows or Cloud Scheduler
question: Which service should run and order these jobs?
quickRule: Airflow for data pipelines with many tasks, Workflows for chaining services, Scheduler for a simple time trigger.

options.name: Managed Service for Apache Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer)
options.chooseWhen: You orchestrate data pipelines, especially ETL or ELT. You write the tasks and the schedule in Python as DAG files.
options.beCarefulWhen: You need very fast steps. The docs say it is best for batch work that can wait a few seconds between tasks.

options.name: Workflows
options.chooseWhen: You chain HTTP-based services and Google Cloud APIs in a set order. It is serverless and runs steps in milliseconds.
options.beCarefulWhen: You process data in pipelines. It has no backfills or DAG re-runs, which Airflow has.

options.name: Cloud Scheduler
options.chooseWhen: You only need to start something on a time schedule, like a cron job. It needs no code and can call HTTP endpoints or Pub/Sub topics.
options.beCarefulWhen: A job runs. It can run more than once, so make the target safe to repeat.
